title: Client-side Zod validation errors do not gate Save, while inspector-reported errors do — one class of author-time error is advisory, the other blocking
body:
Found while taking the producer census for #6331 (see PR #6979). Filed unassigned as an observation, for PM triage. Not fixed there — out of that card's scope, and not flow-specific.

## The asymmetry

`ResourceEditPage.tsx` has two sources of author-time error, and only one of them gates Save.

**Gated** — issues an inspector reports:

```
// ResourceEditPage.tsx:652
// Blocking author-time issues reported by the scoped inspector (e.g. a CEL
// formula that does not parse) — Save must refuse them rather than publish a
// malformed definition (objectui#4306).
```

```
ResourceEditPage.tsx:1999
disabled={saving || (!createMode && !isDirty) || inspectorBlocking > 0}
ResourceEditPage.tsx:1618   if (inspectorBlocking > 0) return;      // auto-save
ResourceEditPage.tsx:1642   if (!saving && (createMode || isDirty) && inspectorBlocking === 0) {
```

**Not gated** — issues the live client Zod validator reports. `validateMetadataDraft` runs the *same schema the server runs* (`clientValidation.ts` maps `flow` to `FlowSchema`, `object` to `ObjectSchema`, and so on for every wired type, on both the create and the edit door), debounced 200 ms on every keystroke, into `setIssues`. That state feeds the banner, the inline field errors and `previewDiagnostics` — and **nothing else**. `inspectorBlocking` is the only term in the Save gate, and `doSave` itself calls no validator.

So: a draft whose *shape* the contract refuses is Saveable; a draft whose CEL predicate does not parse is not. Both are author-time errors, both are already detected client-side, and the comment quoted above states the intent for the class as a whole ("Save must refuse them rather than publish a malformed definition").

## Why it matters

The consequence is the failure shape #6287 was filed about: a refusal the author meets at save time rather than at a gate. It is milder here than in #6287 — the error IS visible while typing (banner, inline, and for flows an on-canvas badge plus a Problems-panel row, since `flow-problems.ts` maps a `nodes.N.…` path onto the offending node) — so this is "the gate is advisory where a sibling gate is blocking", not "the author is told nothing".

## Scope of the reading, stated

- Read on `origin/main` at `7a5da1414`. Traced by reading every use of `inspectorBlocking` and `displayIssues` in `ResourceEditPage.tsx` and confirming `doSave` (line 1294 onward) contains no validation call.
- Not measured in a browser, and no server was booted — the "the server then refuses it" half is cited from the schema (`FlowSchema.safeParse` on a node missing `label` fails with `invalid_type` at `nodes.0.label`), not from a run.

## What this is NOT asking for

⛔ Not "make every Zod issue block Save" as an obvious fix. There are at least two readings, and choosing between them is triage, not this note:

1. The suppression is deliberate and merely undocumented — e.g. so a stale bundled `@objectstack/spec` can never wedge Save shut on a draft the running server would accept. `clientValidation.ts` already carries a root-cure for exactly that skew (it suppresses "missing required field" for fields the live server marks optional), which is evidence for this reading.
2. It is a real gap, and the fix is to gate Save on client Zod *errors* the same way `inspectorBlocking` gates it.

If (1), the answer is a comment at the Save gate saying why schema issues are advisory — the absence of which is what made this look like a defect from the outside.

Related: #6287 (the save-time-refusal class), #6331 / PR #6979 (where this was found), objectui#4306 (the card that added the inspector-side gate).
